:::: {.neu-statement}
::: {.neu-big}
Every day you make decisions that research could improve.
:::

::: {.neu-sub}
This course helps you ask those questions properly, answer them and publish the answer.
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Ask: 'Think of one thing in your department that colleagues do differently, where nobody knows which way is best. Type it in the chat.' Read two or three answers aloud.

Point: research starts from clinical uncertainty, not from statistics.

Timing: 2 minutes.
:::

::: {.notes}
Weeks 1-2: the question and the evidence. Weeks 3-4: design and bias. Weeks 5-6: data and analysis. Weeks 7-8: ethics, writing and publishing. One session every Saturday, with a week between sessions for homework.

One running example travels with us: fluids in septic shock and 28-day mortality. From Session 5 it continues in the course study, FLUID-ICU.

Timing: 2 minutes.
:::

## This course is Level 1 of three

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:3"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Level 1  (this course)]{.neu-card-title}

- **From question to publication**
- Ask, design, analyse, write and publish
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Level 2  (hands-on)]{.neu-card-title}

- **Statistical modelling in R**
- You run the analyses yourself
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#04242F"}
[Level 3  (advanced)]{.neu-card-title}

- **Advanced methods**
- Workshops on request
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Level 1 is this course. Levels 2 and 3 are for those who want to go further.
:::

::: {.notes}
Level 1 takes you from a clinical question to a paper. In it the trainers run the software and you read and interpret the results. Level 2 teaches statistical modelling in R. Level 3 covers advanced methods on request.

Timing: 1 minute.
:::

## Two things you will produce, each on your own

::: {.neu-intro}
Both are individual work. We guide every step in class.
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:2"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Your research proposal]{.neu-card-title}

- On a question from your own department
- Built one part at a time, Sessions 1 to 7
- Submitted in Session 8
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[A draft manuscript]{.neu-card-title}

- Based on the course study, FLUID-ICU
- We give you the results. You write the paper
- Then you review one colleague's draft
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Proposal: built one part at a time in class, submitted in Session 8. A few volunteers also present theirs (6 minutes each).

Manuscript: FLUID-ICU is a course study of 620 ICU patients with sepsis, with five questions (Q1 to Q5). Each person chooses one, receives its tables and figures, and writes the paper. After Session 8 each person reviews one colleague's draft.

Both are written in English. Vietnamese is accepted if English is impossible.

Briefs: Course/Assignment/proposal\_brief and manuscript\_brief.

Timing: 2 minutes.
:::

## By the end of the course you will be able to

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:4"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Ask and find]{.neu-card-title}

- Turn a problem into a clear question
- Search PubMed and manage references
- Read a paper in 15 minutes
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Design]{.neu-card-title}

- Choose a study design
- Recognise bias
- Read the main effect measures
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[Analyse]{.neu-card-title}

- Plan the data you collect
- Read the results of an analysis
- Interpret a real dataset
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0070C0"}
[Write and publish]{.neu-card-title}

- Plan ethics approval
- Write each section of a paper
- Submit and answer reviewers
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Understand and interpret: you will not be asked to calculate.
:::

::: {.notes}
One card per two-week block. The aim is understanding and interpretation, not calculation.

Ask: 'Which card worries you most? Answer in the chat.' Usually: analyse. Reassure: we go slowly and check understanding often.

Timing: 1 minute.
:::

**KEY MESSAGE** A check every 20 minutes. Extra slides only if time allows.
:::

::: {.notes}
The same rhythm every Saturday: recap, two teaching blocks with checks and short tasks, a 15-minute break, then time to build your proposal or paper.

Each session ends with extra slides that we use only if there is time. You can read them at home.

Timing: 1 minute.
:::

## Build your proposal one part at a time

:::: {.neu-steps}
::: {.neu-step style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Part 1]{.neu-step-label}

- **Sessions 1-2**
- Question, background, aims
:::
::: {.neu-step style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Part 2]{.neu-step-label}

- **Sessions 3-4**
- Design and participants
:::
::: {.neu-step style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[Part 3]{.neu-step-label}

- **Sessions 5-6**
- Data, sample size, analysis plan
:::
::: {.neu-step style="--c:#0070C0"}
[Part 4]{.neu-step-label}

- **Session 7**
- Ethics, feasibility, publication plan
:::
::: {.neu-step style="--c:#055F56"}
[Submit]{.neu-step-label}

- **Session 8**
- Complete proposal
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Your own question, one template, one part every two weeks.
:::

::: {.notes}
In each proposal-builder slot the trainer first fills in the part for the running example on a shared screen. Then you write the same part for your own question.

Template: Course/Templates/Research\_Proposal\_Template.docx (sent by email before Session 1).

Timing: 1 minute.
:::

## Welcome: introduce yourself

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#0D7377"}
WHOLE-CLASS TASK · 6 min
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#0D7377"}
- Type your name, department and profession in the chat
- Add one question you wish research could answer in your department
- Read the other messages: many are possible research topics
- A few of you then say your question with the microphone on
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.neu-side .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
Example message

- Lan, ICU, nurse
- 'Do patients with septic shock need less fluid than we give?'
:::
:::
::::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#0D7377"}
**OUTPUT** One introduction per person in the chat
:::

::: {.notes}
About 30 doctors and nurses join from home. We work as one class: no groups.

Give 3 minutes for typing. Then call on 4-5 people to say their question, and point out shared themes (fluids, sedation, infection, mobilisation, medication safety).

The questions stay in the chat. In Proposal builder 1 people can scroll back to them.

Timing: 6 minutes.
:::

## How we learn together online

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:4"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Ask anything]{.neu-card-title}

- There are no silly questions
- Use the chat or 'raise hand'
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Go slow]{.neu-card-title}

- We check understanding often
- Extra slides only if time allows
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[Bring your department]{.neu-card-title}

- Use examples from your own practice
- No patient names or details
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0070C0"}
[Online habits]{.neu-card-title}

- Camera on when you can
- Microphone off unless speaking
- Back on time after the break
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
This is a safe place to say 'I do not understand'. A private chat message to the trainer is fine.

Chat in Vietnamese or English, whichever helps you think. No patient names or identifiable details.

Timing: 1 minute.
:::

## Pre-course quiz (online form)

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#6C3483"}
QUICK QUIZ · 15 min
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#6C3483"}
- Open the quiz form: the link is in the chat now
- Enter your full name
- 24 multiple-choice questions, one answer each (about 12 minutes)
- Work alone: no notes and no colleagues
- Guess if you are not sure: this is not an exam
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.neu-side .plain style="--c:#6C3483"}
Why a quiz now?

- The same quiz again in Session 8
- We measure the course, not you
:::
:::
::::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#6C3483"}
**OUTPUT** Form submitted
:::

::: {.notes}
Paste the Google Form link in the chat. The form asks for the full name, so the Session 1 and Session 8 answers can be matched.

Participants see no score or answers after submitting. The trainers see the results at once in the form's Responses tab and the linked results sheet.

Close the form after 15 minutes. Do not give the answers today: they are shared after the second attempt in Session 8.

Timing: 15 minutes. Session 1 teaching starts at 0:35 (20:05).

The form is created once from Course/Assessment/google\_form (steps in its README).
:::

# Session 1 · Ask: from clinical problem to research question

## Week 1 · Saturday

- 1.1  Why research? Evidence, study designs, the two course papers
- Break
- 1.2  From problem to question: PICO(T), PECO and FINER
- 1.3  Aims, objectives and hypotheses
- Proposal builder 1: start your own question
- Wrap-up: key words, exit question, homework

::: {.notes}
Session 1 opening (0:35, 20:05), right after the pre-course quiz.

Today's goal: everyone leaves with the start of their own research question, aim and objectives.

The class has little research background and it is evening after work: go slowly and stop at every check.

Timing: 1 minute. Point at the agenda, do not read it.
:::

## 1.1  Why research?

:::: {.neu-statement}
::: {.neu-big}
Why do we need research when we already have experience?
:::

::: {.neu-sub}
35 minutes: evidence, study designs, the two course papers, types of research
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Segment 1.1 (0:35-1:10, 20:05-20:40).

Ask two or three people to answer, microphone on. Expected: experience favours memorable cases, colleagues disagree, practice changes.

Point: experience is good for raising questions, weak for answering them.

Timing: 1 minute.
:::

```

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Experience suggests questions. Fair comparisons in many patients answer them.
:::

::: {.notes}
Left: one clinician, three patients, no comparison group. Right: 50 patients per group, every death counted.

The numbers are illustrative, but the pattern is real: the large CLASSIC trial (NEJM 2022, 1,554 patients) found the same 90-day mortality with restrictive and standard fluids (42.3% vs 42.1%).

Ask: 'Why do we remember the three good outcomes?' Expected: recall bias. Dramatic cases stick, failures are forgotten.

Timing: 4 minutes. The whole course rests on this idea.
:::

## Why one ward's experience is not enough

![](images/figures/sat1/small_numbers.png){.neu-fig}

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Small numbers jump around by chance. Large, fair comparisons settle down.
:::

::: {.notes}
A simulation: the true risk of death is 40%. Top row: 20 wards with 5 patients each, from 0% to 80% deaths by chance alone. Groups of 500 cluster around 40%.

Poll (yes / no / cannot tell): 'One ward lost 0 of 5 patients after a new protocol. Does it work?' Answer: cannot tell. 0 of 5 happens often by chance.

Timing: 4 minutes. Sample size returns in Session 6.
:::

## The evidence pyramid

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
::: {.neu-side-notes}
### How to read it

- Higher = less risk of bias, for questions about treatment effects
- A good cohort can beat a poor trial
- Descriptive questions do not need a trial
:::
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}

::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** The pyramid ranks designs, not individual papers: quality still has to be checked.
:::

::: {.notes}
Build from the bottom: expert opinion, case series, case-control, cohort, randomised trials, and systematic reviews that combine studies.

Higher designs protect better against bias for 'does treatment X work?' questions. A small or badly run trial can still mislead.

For how common, harm and prognosis questions, observational designs are often the right choice.

Timing: 4 minutes. Session 3 covers each design: do not teach designs here.
:::

## Quick quiz: rank the evidence

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#6C3483"}
QUICK QUIZ · 3 min
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#6C3483"}
- The question: do restrictive fluids reduce deaths in septic shock?
- A: a senior colleague: 'In 20 years, my patients kept dry did better'
- B: a registry that followed thousands of ICU patients (a cohort)
- C: a trial that randomly assigned 1,554 patients to restrictive or usual fluids
- D: a systematic review of all trials of fluid restriction
- Poll: which order runs from weakest to strongest?
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.neu-side .plain style="--c:#6C3483"}
Poll options

- A, B, C, D
- B, A, C, D
- A, C, B, D
- D, C, B, A
:::
:::
::::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#6C3483"}
**OUTPUT** Poll result, then: what could make C weaker than B?
:::

::: {.notes}
Give 1 minute, then share the results. Answer: A, B, C, D.

C is the real CLASSIC trial, which found no difference in 90-day mortality.

What could make C weaker than B? Very small, many patients lost, or patients unlike ours.

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

## The two papers we read together in this course

::: {.neu-intro}
Both are open access. You receive the two PDFs by email before Session 1.
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:2"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Paper 1: Boulet 2024, a trial]{.neu-card-title}

- **Boulet N, et al. Crit Care 2024;28:429**
- Impact on fluid balance of an optimized restrictive strategy targeting non-resuscitative fluids in intensive care patients with septic shock
- A small pilot randomised controlled trial (RCT), 48 patients
- Main outcome: fluid balance at day 5
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Paper 2: Hyun 2023, a cohort]{.neu-card-title}

- **Hyun DG, et al. Ann Intensive Care 2023;13:105**
- Impact of a cumulative positive fluid balance during the first three ICU days in patients with sepsis
- A cohort study from the Korean sepsis registry
- Main outcome: death by day 28
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Paper 1 is a trial, Paper 2 is a cohort. Both study fluids in sepsis.
:::

::: {.notes}
We refer to these two papers in every session.

Paper 1: a pilot trial in three French ICUs. A pilot is a small trial that tests whether a larger one is possible. It restricted 'non-resuscitative' fluids (maintenance fluids and fluids used to dilute drugs).

Paper 2: a matched cohort from the Korean Sepsis Alliance registry, like option B in the quiz.

Do not read them now. In Session 2 we read Paper 1's abstract together.

Timing: 2 minutes.

Before Session 1, email the two original PDFs (Course/Papers, files named 'original') with the Session 1 exercise sheet.
:::

0.11292cqw);overflow:visible;text-align:center;align-items:stretch"><div style="font-size:calc(20 * 0.11292cqw);color:#0D7377;font-weight:700">Weeks 1-2</div><div style="font-size:calc(16 * 0.11292cqw);color:#1A1A1A;margin-top:calc(3 * 0.11292cqw)">problem, question, search</div></div></div>
```

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Research is a cycle: published results change practice and raise new questions.
:::

::: {.notes}
One sentence per box. Weeks 1-2 cover the three teal boxes: problem, question, search.

Misconception: 'research = collecting data'. Data come after the question, design and ethics approval.

Timing: 2 minutes.
:::

## The question decides the type of research

| Type of research | What it gives | Example |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Quantitative | Numbers: how many? Does X change Y? | 28-day mortality with two fluid strategies |
| Qualitative | Words: why? How? What is it like? | Interviews: why nurses hesitate to stop fluids |
| Mixed methods | Numbers + words in one study | Survey of fluid practice + focus groups |
| Primary research | You collect new data | Paper 1: a new trial |
| Secondary research | You reuse data that exist: records, registries | Paper 2: a sepsis registry |

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Numbers answer how many and how much. Words answer why and how.
:::

::: {.notes}
First three rows: what kind of data. Last two rows: where the data come from.

Misconception: 'qualitative research is just opinion'. It has its own rigorous methods.

Timing: 3 minutes. Qualitative designs return in Session 3.
:::

## Check your understanding: which type of research?

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#6C3483"}
QUICK QUIZ · 2 min
:::

::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#6C3483"}
- A: counting how many patients with septic shock are fluid-positive on day 3 this year
- B: interviewing ICU nurses about why they hesitate to stop IV fluids
- C: re-analysing 3 years of ICU records for fluid balance and death
- D: a survey of fluid prescribing plus focus groups with doctors
- For each: numbers, words or both? New data or existing data?
:::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#6C3483"}
**OUTPUT** Two or three people answer aloud, e.g. 'A: numbers, new'
:::

::: {.notes}
Call on two or three people for short answers. The answers are on the next slide.

If people hesitate on C: the records were made for care, not for this study, so using them is secondary research.

Timing: 2 minutes.
:::

## Answers: which type of research?

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:4"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[A  Counting]{.neu-card-title}

- Quantitative
- Primary
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[B  Interviews]{.neu-card-title}

- Qualitative
- Primary
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[C  Old records]{.neu-card-title}

- Quantitative
- Secondary
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0070C0"}
[D  Survey + groups]{.neu-card-title}

- Mixed methods
- Primary
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Ask two things: numbers or words? New data or existing data?
:::

::: {.notes}
Two questions classify almost any study: what kind of data, and where they come from.

Secondary research is often the most feasible for a busy department, if the records are good (Session 5).

Timing: 1 minute.
:::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** This course walks the whole road. Your proposal covers stops 1 to 6.
:::

::: {.notes}
Eleven stops. The colours show the weeks that teach each stop.

Stops 1-6 plan and do the study. Stops 7-11 publish it. Trials are registered before the first patient is enrolled. The road often takes one to three years, and many studies stall at stop 7.

Ask: 'At which stop do hospital studies get stuck?' Expected: ethics paperwork, data collection or writing.

Timing: 3 minutes, then 3 minutes for questions. Segment 1.1 ends at 1:10 (20:40).
:::

## 1.2  From problem to question

:::: {.neu-statement}
::: {.neu-big}
A good question is half of the answer.
:::

::: {.neu-sub}
40 minutes: PICO(T) and PECO, question types, FINER, then a whole-class task
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Segment 1.2 (1:25-2:05, 20:55-21:35).

A vague worry ('are fluids bad?') must become a precise question before anything else can happen.

Timing: 30 seconds.
:::

## Where do research questions come from?

::: {.neu-intro}
First check: is the answer already known? The literature search tells you (Session 2).
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:3"}
::: {.neu-card style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Where questions come from]{.neu-card-title}

- Bedside doubt: "Why do we do it this way?"
- Colleagues who do it differently
- Incident and registry data
- Guidelines with "low-certainty evidence"
- Papers that end "more research is needed"
- Questions from patients and families
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[Known]{.neu-card-title}

- **Apply it**
- Update the local guideline or protocol
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#055F56"}
[Not known]{.neu-card-title}

- **Research question**
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** If the answer is known, apply it. If it is not, you have a research question.
:::

::: {.notes}
Six common sources of questions, all from daily work.

Before calling something research, check whether the answer already exists. If it does, the job is to apply it.

Point back to the questions the class typed in the chat at the start.

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

## PICO(T): our running example

::: {.neu-intro}
In adults with septic shock in the ICU, does a restrictive fluid strategy, compared with usual care, reduce 28-day mortality?
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:5"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[P  Population]{.neu-card-title}

- Adults (18+) with septic shock in the ICU
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[I  Intervention]{.neu-card-title}

- Restrictive fluid strategy
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[C  Comparison]{.neu-card-title}

- Usual care (standard fluids)
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0070C0"}
[O  Outcome]{.neu-card-title}

- Death from any cause
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#8A99A3"}
[T  Time]{.neu-card-title}

- Within 28 days
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Every session we come back to this one question.
:::

::: {.notes}
PICO = Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome. T (Time) says when the outcome is measured.

Each letter forces a decision: which patients, restrictive how, compared with what, which outcome and when?

Ask: 'Is 28-day mortality the only sensible outcome?' Expected: 90-day mortality, kidney injury needing dialysis, fluid balance.

Timing: 4 minutes.
:::

## Three more examples: PICO, PECO and P + O

| P | I / E | C | O | T |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Treatment (PICO) | Ventilated adults in the ICU | Twice-daily bed-head checklist | Usual care | Ventilator-associated pneumonia | ICU day 28 |
| Risk factor (PECO) E = Exposure | Adults on the medical ward | Obesity (BMI 30+) | BMI under 30 | New pressure injury | During admission |
| How common? (P + O) | Adults 65+ after hip surgery | - | - | Delirium | First 7 days |

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** PECO: E = Exposure, used when we cannot assign the factor (e.g. obesity).
:::

::: {.notes}
Three examples from other wards. PECO is PICO with E (Exposure) in place of I: something patients have that the researcher does not assign, such as obesity or a positive fluid balance.

Row 3 only needs P and O (and T): it asks how common something is.

Ask: 'Make a PECO question about fluids.' Expected: in adults with sepsis, is a positive fluid balance by day 3, compared with a neutral or negative balance, associated with death by day 28? This is Paper 2's question.

Timing: 4 minutes.
:::

## Check your understanding: spot the PICO

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#6C3483"}
QUICK QUIZ · 3 min
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#6C3483"}
- Paper 1's question: 'In adults with septic shock in the first 24 hours of vasopressors, does restricting non-resuscitative fluids, compared with usual care, reduce cumulative fluid balance at day 5?'
- Poll: which words are the outcome (O)?
- Then two or three people say the population (P)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.neu-side .plain style="--c:#6C3483"}
Poll options

- A: septic shock
- B: restricting non-resuscitative fluids
- C: cumulative fluid balance
- D: day 5
:::
:::
::::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#6C3483"}
**OUTPUT** Poll answer, then P said aloud
:::

::: {.notes}
Read the question slowly. Give 1 minute for the poll. Answer: C. D is the time (T), A is part of P, B is I.

Watch for 'septic shock' chosen as the outcome: it has already happened, so it defines who is eligible.

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:5"}

- Usual care
:::

[O]{.neu-card-title}

- Cumulative fluid balance
:::

[T]{.neu-card-title}

- Day 5
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** The condition that brings patients in (septic shock) is part of P, not O.
:::

::: {.notes}
The outcome must be something that can happen after the intervention starts.

Paper 1's outcome is fluid balance, not death, so it cannot answer our 28-day mortality question.

Timing: 2 minutes.
:::

## Two families of questions

::: {.neu-intro}
The question decides the design (more in Session 3).
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:3"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[Descriptive]{.neu-card-title}

- What? How many? Who?
- "How many of our septic shock patients have a positive fluid balance on day 3?"
- **Case series, cross-sectional**
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Analytical: observe]{.neu-card-title}

- Is X linked to Y?
- "Is a positive fluid balance associated with death?"
- **Cohort, case-control**
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#055F56"}
[Analytical: intervene]{.neu-card-title}

- Does X cause Y?
- "Does restricting fluids reduce 28-day mortality?"
- **Randomised controlled trial**
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Descriptive questions describe. Analytical questions compare or test a cause.
:::

::: {.notes}
The verbs give it away: 'how many' is descriptive, 'is associated with' is observational, 'does it reduce' implies a trial.

Ask: 'Paper 2: which box?' Expected: analytical, observe (a cohort).

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

## From a vague worry to an answerable question

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:2"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#B23B2E"}
[Vague]{.neu-card-title}

- **"Are fluids bad for ICU patients?"**
- Which patients?
- Which fluid, how much?
- Bad compared with what?
- Bad how? By when?
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#2E8B57"}
[Answerable, with PICO]{.neu-card-title}

- P: In adults with septic shock in the ICU,
- I: does a restrictive fluid strategy,
- C: compared with usual care,
- O: reduce mortality
- T: at 28 days?
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** If you cannot fill all the PICO boxes, the question is not ready yet.
:::

::: {.notes}
Left: the corridor question, every word undefined. Right: the same worry written with PICO(T).

Ask: 'Make this answerable: Is albumin better?' Expected: in adults with septic shock, does albumin plus crystalloid, compared with crystalloid alone, reduce 28-day mortality?

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

## FINER: is the question worth asking?

::: {.neu-intro}
Check every question against five tests before you invest time in it.
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:5"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[F  Feasible]{.neu-card-title}

- Enough patients
- Time, money and skills
- Data you can get
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[I  Interesting]{.neu-card-title}

- To you and your team
- To readers
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[N  Novel]{.neu-card-title}

- Confirms, refutes or extends what is known
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0070C0"}
[E  Ethical]{.neu-card-title}

- An ethics committee could approve it
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#055F56"}
[R  Relevant]{.neu-card-title}

- Could change practice, policy or research
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** If the question fails one letter, rewrite it before going further.
:::

::: {.notes}
FINER = Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical, Relevant (Hulley, Designing Clinical Research).

Feasible fails most often in hospital research: too few patients, or an outcome that is too rare.

Novel does not mean 'never studied': a new setting or a better design can be novel.

Poll (F, I, N, E, R): 'Which letter does our running example fail?'

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

## FINER check of our running example

::: {.neu-intro}
Restrictive fluids vs usual care in septic shock: 28-day mortality, in your own ICU.
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:5"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#B23B2E"}
[F  Feasible]{.neu-card-title}

- **[Red]{style="color:#B23B2E"}**
- Mortality needs more than 1,000 patients
- Too big for one ICU
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#2E8B57"}
[I  Interesting]{.neu-card-title}

- **[Green]{style="color:#2E8B57"}**
- Fluids are debated on every ward round
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#D9822B"}
[N  Novel]{.neu-card-title}

- **[Amber]{style="color:#D9822B"}**
- Large trials have already been done
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#D9822B"}
[E  Ethical]{.neu-card-title}

- **[Amber]{style="color:#D9822B"}**
- Both strategies are used today
- Consent in the ICU needs care
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#2E8B57"}
[R  Relevant]{.neu-card-title}

- **[Green]{style="color:#2E8B57"}**
- Every patient with septic shock gets fluid
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Important, but too big for one ICU. Next: make it smaller.
:::

::: {.notes}
F is red: a difference of a few percentage points in mortality needs well over a thousand patients. The CLASSIC (2022) and CLOVERS (2023) trials each randomised more than 1,500.

N is amber: those large trials found no difference in mortality. E is amber: consent in septic shock is hard (Session 7).

To make it smaller: change the outcome, run a pilot trial as Paper 1 did, or ask a descriptive question. The next slide does exactly this.

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

## Whole-class task: rescue our running example

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#0D7377"}
WHOLE-CLASS TASK · 11 min
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#0D7377"}
- Open Exercise 1 on the Session 1 exercise sheet
- It gives three smaller versions of the question: A, B and C (right)
- Poll: which version could your ICU do within two years?
- For the chosen version, people called on give P, I or E, C, O and T
- Together: name the question type and colour each FINER letter
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.neu-side .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
The three versions

- A: restrictive protocol vs usual care, fluid balance at day 5 (a pilot trial)
- B: fluid-positive by day 3 or not, death by day 28 (a cohort)
- C: how many of your patients are fluid-positive on day 3? (descriptive)
:::
:::
::::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#0D7377"}
**OUTPUT** One class question with PICO(T) and FINER colours, typed on the shared screen
:::

::: {.notes}
Share a blank Exercise 1 and type the answers as people give them, one person per letter.

Most classes choose A or C. If the vote is split, take A: it is the pilot that Paper 1 ran, and the quick exercise in 1.3 uses it.

Version B is a PECO question (fluid balance is an exposure). It is the main question of the FLUID-ICU course study.

Common problems: no comparison, an outcome without a time point, two outcomes in one question.

Model answers: Course/Solutions/s1\_solutions.md, Exercise 1.

Timing: 8 minutes work + 3 minutes summary. Segment 1.3 starts at 2:05 (21:35).
:::

## 1.3  Aims, objectives, hypotheses

:::: {.neu-statement}
::: {.neu-big}
A question says what we want to know. Aims and objectives say what we will do.
:::

::: {.neu-sub}
20 minutes: aim, objectives, hypotheses and one quick exercise
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Segment 1.3 (2:05-2:25, 21:35-21:55).

The aim, objectives and hypothesis are the question written as a plan. Ethics committees read them first.

Timing: 30 seconds.
:::

## Aim and objectives: our running example

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:2"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#055F56"}
[Aim]{.neu-card-title}

- **The broad why, in one sentence**
- To compare a restrictive fluid strategy with usual care in adults with septic shock in the ICU
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Objectives]{.neu-card-title}

- **The specific what, with measurable verbs**
- Primary: compare 28-day mortality
- Compare fluid balance at day 5
- Compare kidney injury needing dialysis
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** One aim, 2-3 measurable objectives. Mark the primary one.
:::

::: {.notes}
The aim is the broad purpose ('To compare...', 'To describe...'). The objectives are specific, measurable steps.

Mark the primary objective: it decides the sample size (Session 6).

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

## Objectives start with a measurable verb

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:2"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#B23B2E"}
[Vague verbs]{.neu-card-title}

- understand, know, study, explore, look at
- "To understand fluid management in our ICU"
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#2E8B57"}
[Measurable verbs]{.neu-card-title}

- compare, estimate, describe, determine, measure
- "To compare cumulative fluid balance at day 5 between the two groups"
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** If you cannot say how you will measure it, it is not yet an objective.
:::

::: {.notes}
'To understand' can never be finished or checked. 'To compare fluid balance at day 5' names the outcome, the time and the comparison.

Ask: 'Rewrite: to study fluid balance in our ICU.' Expected: to estimate the proportion of adults with septic shock in our ICU who have a positive fluid balance on day 3.

Timing: 3 minutes.
:::

## Null and alternative hypotheses

::: {.neu-intro}
A hypothesis predicts the answer to the primary objective: compare 28-day mortality.
:::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** We test H0. Data can reject it or fail to reject it, but never prove it.
:::

::: {.notes}
H0, the null hypothesis: no difference. H1, the alternative: a difference, in either direction.

Analogy: a court assumes 'not guilty' (H0) until the evidence is strong enough. 'Not guilty' is not 'innocent'.

Purely descriptive questions (version C) estimate a number and need no hypothesis.

Timing: 3 minutes. P-values are Session 6.
:::

## Quick exercise: aim, objectives and hypothesis for the pilot

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#0B376C"}
INDIVIDUAL TASK · 7 min
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#0B376C"}
- The pilot question (version A): in adults with septic shock, does a restrictive fluid protocol, compared with usual care, reduce cumulative fluid balance at day 5?
- Write one aim: 'To compare...'
- Write two objectives with measurable verbs. Mark the primary one
- Write H0 and H1 for the primary objective
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.neu-side .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
Verbs that work

- compare
- estimate
- describe
- determine
- measure
:::
:::
::::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#0B376C"}
**OUTPUT** Exercise 2 on the exercise sheet. Two or three people read theirs aloud
:::

::: {.notes}
5 minutes writing alone, then 2 minutes for two or three people to read their primary objective.

Look for vague verbs, no time point, or a hypothesis about an outcome that is not in the objectives.

Timing: 7 minutes.
:::

## Model answer: the pilot question

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:3"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Aim]{.neu-card-title}

- To compare a restrictive fluid protocol with usual care in adults with septic shock in your ICU
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Objectives]{.neu-card-title}

- Primary: to compare cumulative fluid balance at day 5 between groups
- Secondary: to estimate the recruitment rate and protocol adherence
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[Hypothesis]{.neu-card-title}

- H0: fluid balance at day 5 is the same in both groups
- H1: it differs between the groups
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Aim, primary objective and hypothesis all name the same outcome.
:::

::: {.notes}
Check the chain: the question's O = the primary objective = the outcome in H0 and H1. Reviewers spot a break at once.

Model answers: Course/Solutions/s1\_solutions.md (Exercise 2).

Timing: 3 minutes. Segment 1.3 ends at 2:25 (21:55).
:::

## Proposal builder 1: your own question

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#055F56"}
PROPOSAL BUILDER · 30 min
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#055F56"}
- Watch: we fill Part 1 of the template for the running example
- Open your copy of the proposal template
- Choose one problem from your own department
- Write your PICO(T) question and check it with FINER
- Add one aim, 2-3 objectives (mark the primary) and H0/H1
- Two volunteers read their question aloud
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}

Timing

- 0-8 min: we model Part 1
- 8-25 min: you draft your own
- 25-30 min: two volunteers share

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#055F56"}
**OUTPUT** Proposal Part 1 started: question, FINER check, aim, objectives, hypothesis
:::

Minutes 0-8: share Course/Templates/Research\_Proposal\_Template.docx and fill Part 1 for version A, thinking aloud.

Minutes 8-25: everyone drafts alone. Cameras may go off. Answer questions in the chat.

No topic yet? Look back at the questions in the welcome chat, or use version A or C for now.

Minutes 25-30: two volunteers read their question and aim. Others suggest one improvement each.

Timing: 30 minutes. Wrap-up starts at 2:55 (22:25).

## Key words of the day

| Key word | In one line |
|:---|:---|
| Evidence pyramid | Ranks designs by how well they protect against bias |
| PICO(T) | Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Time |
| PECO | The same, with E = Exposure, for factors we do not assign |
| FINER | Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical, Relevant |
| Aim / objective | The broad why / the specific, measurable what |
| H0 / H1 | No difference / a difference (we test H0) |

::: {.notes}
Wrap-up (2:55-3:00, 22:25-22:30). Read the six key words quickly. They are in the course glossary (EN-VN).

Timing: 1 minute.
:::

## Session 1 recap

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:3"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Why research]{.neu-card-title}

- Experience suggests questions
- Fair comparisons in enough patients answer them
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Ask precisely]{.neu-card-title}

- A PICO(T) question
- One primary outcome
- A FINER check before you start
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[Plan it]{.neu-card-title}

- One aim
- 2-3 measurable objectives
- A testable H0 and H1
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Next Saturday: find and read what is already known about your question.
:::

::: {.notes}
Next Saturday (Session 2) we search PubMed live, manage references in Zotero and read a paper in 15 minutes.

Timing: 1 minute.

## Exit question (in the chat)

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#6C3483"}
QUICK QUIZ · 2 min
:::

::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#6C3483"}
- Answer in the chat before you leave
- Q1: which FINER letter did our running example fail, and why?
- Q2: rewrite as an objective: 'To understand fluid balance in our ICU'
:::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#6C3483"}
**OUTPUT** One short answer per person in the chat
:::

::: {.notes}
Not marked. Answers: Q1 Feasible: mortality needs well over a thousand patients. Q2 e.g. 'To estimate the proportion of adults with septic shock in our ICU who have a positive fluid balance on day 3'.

Save the chat and read the answers during the week. If many still use vague verbs, start Session 2 with one minute on objectives.

Timing: 2 minutes.
:::

## Research, audit or quality improvement?

| Research | Clinical audit | Quality improvement |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Asks | What is the best practice? | Are we meeting the standard? | How do we get better, step by step? |
| Fluid example | Restrictive vs usual: which is better? | Is fluid balance recorded daily? | A daily checklist, tested in small cycles |
| Results apply to | Patients elsewhere | Our unit | Our unit |
| Ethics | **[Ethics committee approval: always]{style="color:#B23B2E"}** | Local approval, usually no committee | Local approval, ethics review if new risk |

::: {.neu-table-caption}
Not sure which it is? Ask the ethics committee before you start.
:::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Research asks what is best. Audit asks if we do it. QI makes it better.
:::

::: {.notes}
Extra, for when someone asks whether their project needs ethics approval.

Audit compares practice with an agreed standard. Quality improvement (QI) changes a local process in small Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles. If a project randomises, adds a new risk or collects data beyond routine care, it is research.

Rules differ between institutions: check the local policy. Ethics approval is Session 7.

Timing: 3 minutes if used.
:::

## Extra: the three examples as research questions

::: {.neu-intro}
Backup for 'Three more examples': write the question for each row, then compare.
:::

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:3"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Treatment (PICO)]{.neu-card-title}

- In ventilated adults in the ICU, does a twice-daily bed-head checklist, compared with usual care, reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia by ICU day 28?
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Risk factor (PECO)]{.neu-card-title}

- In adults on the medical ward, is obesity (BMI 30 or more), compared with a BMI under 30, associated with new pressure injury during the admission?
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[How common? (P + O)]{.neu-card-title}

- In adults aged 65 or over after hip surgery, how common is delirium in the first 7 days?
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Each question names the patients, the comparison (if any), the outcome and the time.
:::

::: {.notes}
Backup slide for 'Three more examples: PICO, PECO and P + O' (reviewer request).

Use it as a short exercise: participants write one question per row in the chat, or you call on two or three people (microphone on). Then show this slide.

Point out: the treatment question says 'reduce' because the checklist is assigned. The PECO question says 'associated with' because obesity is not assigned. The 'how common' question has no comparison.

Timing: 5 minutes if used.
:::

## PICO for other kinds of question

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:3"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0D7377"}
[Diagnosis]{.neu-card-title}

- P: patients tested
- I: the new test
- C: the reference standard
- O: accuracy
- Example: in suspected sepsis in the emergency department, how accurate is qSOFA compared with Sepsis-3?
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#0B376C"}
[Prognosis]{.neu-card-title}

- P: patients with a condition
- E: a risk factor
- O: what happens
- T: by when
- Example: in septic shock, is a lactate above 4 mmol/L on admission linked to death by day 28?
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#5FA39B"}
[Qualitative (SPIDER)]{.neu-card-title}

- S: Sample
- PI: Phenomenon of Interest
- D: Design
- E: Evaluation, R: Research type
- Example: how do ICU nurses experience stopping IV fluids, in interviews?
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** The letters change, but the idea stays the same: be explicit.
:::

::: {.notes}
Extra. Diagnosis: the new test is I, the reference standard is C, the outcome is accuracy (Session 4).

Prognosis: PECO plus a time frame. Qualitative questions often use SPIDER (Cooke and colleagues, 2012).

Timing: 2 minutes if used.
:::

## More practice: which FINER letter fails?

::: {.neu-banner style="--c:#6C3483"}
QUICK QUIZ · 4 min
:::

::: {.neu-activity-steps style="--c:#6C3483"}
- All hospitalised adults in the country: does vitamin D reduce mortality over 10 years?
- Septic shock: does withholding antibiotics for 24 h reduce resistance?
- Do our ICU nurses wash their hands? (audited monthly for 5 years)
- Pneumonia: does the colour of the drug chart affect 28-day mortality?
:::

::: {.neu-output style="--c:#6C3483"}
**OUTPUT** One letter per question, in the poll
:::

::: {.notes}
Extra. Answers: 1 Feasible (huge and long). 2 Ethical (withholding antibiotics causes harm). 3 Novel (already measured every month). 4 Relevant (no plausible effect on practice).

Timing: 4 minutes if used.
:::

## Vague vs answerable: another example from the ward

:::: {.neu-cards style="--n:2"}
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#B23B2E"}
[Vague]{.neu-card-title}

- **"Do night shifts cause medication errors?"**
- Which staff?
- Compared with what?
- Which errors, counted how?
- Over what period?
:::
::: {.neu-card .plain style="--c:#2E8B57"}
[Answerable, with PECO]{.neu-card-title}

- P: In ward nurses,
- E: are night shifts,
- C: compared with day shifts,
- O: linked to more errors per 1,000 doses
- T: over 6 months?
:::
::::

::: {.neu-takeaway}
**KEY MESSAGE** Practise on your own ward: take a corridor question and fill the boxes.
:::

::: {.notes}
Extra. This is a PECO (observational) question: nurses cannot easily be randomised to night shifts.

Timing: 3 minutes if used.
:::
